extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers preparing manuscripts for The American Naturalist
extracted.subtask_description: A recommended (optional) checklist for authors and reviewers to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and journal-appropriate presentation for manuscripts submitted to The American Naturalist, covering general, empirical, meta-analysis, theory, and formatting concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for The American Naturalist
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript causes readers to consider new ideas, merge existing ideas in new ways, rethink familiar ideas, or provides particularly compelling evidence for established ideas; theory and data papers are welcome in equal measure; methods papers enable new questions or address existing questions in particularly effective ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the submission fits the journal's aims: novelty (broadly construed), synthetic insight, strong empirical support, or methods that advance the field. This is a high-level filter for suitability rather than a scoring rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript gives sufficient coverage to relevant existing ideas and does not inflate its own novelty by omitting mention of relevant published studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may cite reviews and syntheses, but when possible should also cite original sources for key new insights. Ensure key prior work is acknowledged so claims of novelty are justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality, length, and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be thorough but succinct: as long as they need to be, and not one word longer; prose should be clear, free from typographical errors, spelling and grammar mistakes, and structured in well-organized sentences and paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should refrain from commenting on presumed linguistic qualifications of authors. Ensure clarity and concise exposition; avoid unnecessary verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure color accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures avoid use of red/green that may be hard for color blind readers to see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use color palettes accessible to color-blind readers; prefer color choices that clearly distinguish lines/groups without relying on red/green contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure and table readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure font sizes and lines are large enough to be easily readable when reproduced on a printed page at a typical figure size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check reproduction legibility: axis labels, tick labels, legends and line widths should remain readable at publication size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure simplicity and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should convey a result as simply and directly as possible, focusing readers’ attention on key trends; figures need not show all data broken down in all possible ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overcomplicated multi-panel figures that obscure the main message. Use color where appropriate to distinguish lines and emphasize key comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials should not hold core message
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary Materials enrich the results but are not essential elements to understand the core message of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imagine if the Supplement were lost to history, 50 years from now, would the paper still be understandable? If not, move essential elements into the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approvals and conservation impact
rubrics_metrics.description: For vertebrate animal research, authors describe animal care approval; for human subjects, authors describe institutional research approval (e.g., IRB); the research does not pose a threat to population viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state ethical approvals and justify that the study does not endanger populations. Include permit and oversight details where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field study permits, locations, and dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors report information about collecting permits (if needed), list specific locations (e.g., coordinates) where samples were collected or experiments performed (with exceptions to protect threatened populations), and report dates of the field work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient spatiotemporal detail to allow interpretation and possible future replication, while allowing exceptions for sensitive locations/species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent transparency (planned vs post-hoc analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to state whether the research was initially planned to address the topic reported in the paper, or whether the paper is reporting on post-hoc analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about whether analyses were planned a priori or arose from post-hoc exploration. This transparency helps readers and reviewers evaluate strength of inference. (Marked as aspirational ✪.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-registration disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a study design was pre-registered, authors are encouraged to state whether the study design was pre-registered; the journal does not require pre-registration nor penalize its absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State pre-registration details and any deviations from the plan. Even if not pre-registered, acknowledge when analyses are post-hoc versus pre-planned. (Marked as aspirational ✪.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling allocation and sample size rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors report how study subjects were allocated to experimental treatments and state how sample sizes were chosen (e.g., describe a power analysis, or logistical constraints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear rationale for sample sizes and randomization/allocation procedures so analyses can be properly interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genetic stock sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, sources of genetic stocks are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report provenance of genetic lines, strains, or populations used so results are interpretable and reproducible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental treatment magnitudes and selection rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state the magnitude of experimental treatments (e.g., food rations, pH levels), and describe how these magnitudes were chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain biological or logistical basis for chosen treatment levels to justify relevance and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding of observers
rubrics_metrics.description: Observers recording data were blind to the experimental treatment imposed on the research subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether and how blinding was implemented to reduce observer bias; if blinding was not possible, describe mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voucher specimen deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If voucher specimens are available, authors identify where they are deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide repository names, accession numbers, or other identifiers to enable future verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed protocols for non-standard methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provide detailed protocols for non-standard methods as supplementary materials, to aid readers in exactly replicating these methods, including reagents, concentrations, plasticware, vendors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include step-by-step details sufficient for replication; place lengthy technical details in Supplement but ensure core methodological clarity is in main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report sample sizes for all datasets and subsets
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors report sample sizes for all data, including subsets of data (e.g., each treatment group, other subsets), and sample size used for all statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State n for every analysis and subgroup so readers can assess power and scope; avoid vague statements like 'small sample size' without numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify level of replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors identify the level of replication relevant to a given analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether replication is at the individual, population, experimental unit, or other level, and ensure analyses reflect the correct replication unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details of data analysis (software, packages, tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provide the precise details of data analysis (software, packages with citations to authors, and descriptions of each statistical test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List software versions, packages (with citations), and the exact procedures/tests used so analyses can be reproduced and evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect sizes and uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors provide estimates of effect size, and uncertainty in these estimates. Tests of statistical significance that omit effect sizes are omitting the biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report effect sizes (e.g., means differences, regression coefficients) with confidence intervals or other uncertainty metrics; do not rely solely on p-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory analyses disclosure and model selection rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: If exploratory analyses were performed, then only a subset of models reported in the paper, all exploratory analyses should be acknowledged, and the choice of final focal models clearly explained. In reporting model results, estimated effects for all model variables should be reported (this may be in Supplementary materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish exploratory from confirmatory analyses; explain model selection and report full parameter estimates to allow assessment of model robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code availability for analysis replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Code to replicate data analysis should be made available for both review and for readers after publication. (Marked as aspirational ✪.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide well-documented code with dependencies and instructions. Sharing code aids reproducibility; if sharing via a website that reveals reviewer identity, use attachments or anonymized repositories per journal guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis scope identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors identify the scope of the meta-analysis: range of dates, geography, taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state inclusion boundaries so readers understand the domain and limits of inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis search criteria and keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors describe the search criteria used to obtain information, including databases and keywords. Keyword searches include antonyms to catch negative effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full search strings, databases searched, and any strategies used to detect negative/contrary findings; help ensure comprehensive and unbiased literature capture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors describe criteria for including or excluding studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide objective, reproducible criteria and justify subjective decisions; report how many studies excluded for each reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis data extraction and repeatability
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors describe how data was extracted from relevant studies, include software citations where relevant, and state whether duplicate observers obtain replicate data extracts to evaluate repeatability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe extraction protocols, training, and any inter-observer checks; indicate use of multiple extractors or arbitration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis pre-registration encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to acknowledge whether the study design was pre-registered. There is no penalty for lack of pre-registration. (Marked as aspirational ✪.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State pre-registration details if present; absence is acceptable but noting it aids transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis effect size measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state measures of effect size used in the meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the effect size metric and justify its appropriateness for the question and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis study weighting and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state methods for weighting studies by confidence, or justify the lack thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain weighting schemes (e.g., inverse variance) or reasons for unweighted analyses; discuss implications for results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis pseudoreplication handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state how analyses accounted for pseudoreplication arising from multiple effect size estimates within one study population or species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe hierarchical/multilevel models or other approaches used to account for non-independence of effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phylogenetic correction in meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Were phylogenetic corrections applied to adjust for non-independence of study species?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If species-level non-independence is relevant, report whether and how phylogenetic relationships were modeled and justify choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis model choices and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors clearly explain statistical model choices, state whether any data points were excluded after data acquisition and why, and explain how many entries suffer from missing data and how these missing data were handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale for model structure, document exclusions and missing-data approaches (imputation, omission), and assess sensitivity to these choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis publication bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: How was publication bias evaluated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funnel plots, trim-and-fill, p-curve, or other diagnostics and report results and sensitivity analyses regarding publication bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-analysis results reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors state the number of studies that passed various filters for inclusion, provide measures of both effect size, variance in effect size, and confidence, and describe possible sources of bias in the available data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report flow of studies through filtering, summary effect estimates with variance/confidence, and candid discussion of dataset limitations and biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: biological motive and empirical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: All theory published should aim to explain or anticipate a biological phenomenon, and must clearly describe the underlying biology with suitable references; authors should describe specific examples and relate model assumptions to biological examples and put results into biological context comparing model output to relevant empirical data when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly connect abstract models to biological systems, provide examples, and, where feasible, compare model predictions to data to demonstrate relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model construction rationale and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors explain rationale behind choosing analytical versus simulation methods, deterministic versus stochastic models, justify choice of continuous versus discrete time, define all symbols where they are first used (tables of symbols are useful), choose functions based on empirical trends when possible, and clearly state and justify assumptions and simplifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification for methodological choices and ensure notation and assumptions are clearly presented so non-specialist readers can follow the model's structure and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: To reach an empirical audience, the meaning of each equation must be clearly summarized in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompany mathematical expressions with plain-language explanations of their biological meaning to aid cross-disciplinary comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model analysis: parameter ranges and exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: The range of parameters is clearly stated and, when possible, justified with reference to biological information; when multiple parameters are involved, parameter space is explored sufficiently widely to evaluate interactions among key parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report parameter bounds, empirical justification, and conduct sensitivity analyses or broad sweeps to assess robustness across plausible parameter space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical solutions and approximations
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical solutions are clearly derived; approximations and simplifications are clearly identified, and their consequences are discussed (e.g., when assuming very weak selection to obtain an analytical result, consider what the consequences are if selection is strong).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document derivations and explicitly discuss limitations and potential failures of approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation code sharing for theory work
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulation code should be made available to reviewers, and subsequently shared on a public repository. Note that sharing your Github page can reveal your identity, so submitting a code file as an attachment with your manuscript is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide runnable, documented simulation code; consider anonymization for peer review, and public hosting after acceptance to maximize reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting required for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous line numbers or page numbers and line numbers are required for peer review; manuscripts must be double-spaced; fonts for math should be embedded in the pdf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these minimal formatting requirements to facilitate reviewer comments and ensure display fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final accepted versions must follow journal citation formatting; methods should always be described before Results; authors are encouraged to put figures and tables in the main text where they are first mentioned, with captions on the same page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial submissions need not perfectly match journal style, but deviations may bias reviewers. Prefer figures near first mention and captions on same page to aid reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof-read your code as carefully as you proof-read your manuscript prose. Code should be carefully annotated to state dependencies, and the purpose of each step. Code should be self-contained so a user with the relevant input data files can re-create your results, without extraneous code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate dependencies, purpose, and ensure reproducibility; follow examples of best-practices (links provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code submission encouragement and privacy caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly encourage authors, when feasible, to submit data tables and analytical code (e.g. an R markdown file) alongside the manuscript, or via a link to a github repository or equivalent; data shared through a website that might reveal reviewer identity will not be accepted and the paper may be returned. Authors are encouraged to have their Dryad data package prepared before submission and to make these files available for review. (Marked as aspirational ✪.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data and code to facilitate review and reuse, but avoid revealing author identity during peer review; prepare archival data packages for final publication.
